localRules.heading: Local rules that affect irrigation
localRules.intro: The CRD sets the outdoor watering schedule for properties on the regional water supply. Here is what matters for a controller.

items.text: CRD Stage 1 runs May 1 to September 30. Lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm.
Hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day.
Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.
The rules apply only where a property is connected to the regional supply; many rural properties use wells.

localRules.areasLink: See how the rules apply where you live on our [service area pages](/areas/).

faqs.q: When should I winterize my irrigation system?
faqs.a: Usually in October or early November, before the first hard frost. Read our [irrigation start-up and winterization guide](/resources/irrigation-start-up-and-winterization/).

faqs.q: Does drip irrigation follow the same watering days?
faqs.a: Under CRD Stage 1 rules, drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day; lawn sprinkling has set days and times. Check the current rules on the [CRD site](https://www.crd.ca/environment/water-conservation/watering-schedule).

faqs.q: Which lawn days apply to a strata complex?
faqs.a: The [CRD watering schedule](https://www.crd.ca/environment/water-conservation/watering-schedule) says multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address, not each unit's number. We set the controller to match.

faqs.q: Can you repair a system someone else installed?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you know about the system when you request a quote, and photos of the controller and valve box help.

faqs.q: Do the CRD rules apply if I am on a well?
faqs.a: The [CRD schedule](https://www.crd.ca/environment/water-conservation/watering-schedule) applies to properties on the regional water supply. Many rural properties in Highlands and Metchosin use wells; confirm your supply before assuming either way.
